content: Exercise caution and closely monitor for additive anticholinergic effects and potential hypoglycemia. Hyoscyamine reduces zotepine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, hyoscyamine decreases zotepine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Adverse effects associated with hyoscyamine include dry skin, blurred vision, constipation, dysphagia, photosensitivity, headache, orthostatic hypotension, tachycardia, xerostomia, urinary hesitancy or retention, hypertension, respiratory depression, central nervous system stimulation, fever, ataxia, excitation, lethargy, palpitations, mydriasis, cycloplegia, increased intraocular pressure, weakness, bloated sensation, suppression of lactation, impotence, and anhidrosis. Hypersensitivity to hyoscyamine or related compounds may occur. Contraindications include closed-angle glaucoma, myasthenia gravis, hemorrhage with cardiovascular instability, paralytic ileus, intestinal atony in elderly or debilitated patients, obstructive uropathy, toxic megacolon, gastrointestinal obstruction, and tachycardia secondary to cardiac insufficiency or thyrotoxicosis. Breastfeeding is not recommended as hyoscyamine enters breast milk. Discontinue treatment if diarrhea occurs, as it may indicate incomplete intestinal obstruction, particularly in patients with colostomy or ileostomy. Hyoscyamine may cause drowsiness; patients should be cautioned against performing hazardous tasks, such as driving or operating heavy machinery, that require mental alertness. Use caution in hot weather or during exercise, as heat prostration has been reported in the presence of elevated environmental temperatures. Psychosis has been reported in patients susceptible to anticholinergic effects, typically resolving within 12–48 hours after discontinuation of therapy. Exercise caution in patients with hyperthyroidism, prostatic hyperplasia, renal impairment, hiatal hernia, or cardiovascular disease, including heart failure, tachyarrhythmias, hypertension, or coronary artery disease. Evaluate tachycardia prior to initiating therapy. Hyoscyamine is classified as Pregnancy Category C. It is generally not recommended during lactation due to its presence in breast milk. The drug is dialyzable and can be removed via hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis. The majority of the drug is excreted unchanged in the urine.
